additional_info.subject: Re: ID0445578-DC/Si-D/IE-[MP / S2 170003301] Connector Faults CRM:02681000680
additional_info.body:
Hi Adam,
In addition to the below;
We welcome the proposed update and will be happy to schedule a maintenance window to apply it, tonight at 1am would be fine.
That said, I must also record that the event on 22 August caused a service outage of approximately 4 hours and resulted in at least one direct customer complaint (William Joyce), who was billed but unable to charge. Under our SLA, Siemens committed to a 2-hour qualified response and 4-hour mobilisation (24/7/365). The response time on this incident fell well short of those terms.
Before we close this ticket, we would appreciate Siemens’ confirmation on the following points:
Corrective action: Please confirm that firmware v8.0.5 / SECC adapter 1.4.11 will be proactively rolled out to all of our chargers, including Galway Retail and the upcoming Sandy Road hub, to ensure stability.
Customer compensation: Please confirm whether Siemens will directly pay us for the lost revenue on this session and how we are to manage these situations.
SLA performance: Please explain why the SLA commitments of 2-hour response / 4-hour mobilisation were not met, and what measures Siemens will put in place to ensure service levels are achieved going forward.
We appreciate your technical resolution, but we must also ensure that service accountability and customer impact are addressed as part of our ongoing partnership.
Colin Barry
Brite EV charging

additional_info.subject: ID0445578-DC/Si-D/IE-[MP / S2 170003301] Connector Faults CRM:02681000680
additional_info.body:
Hello Colin, good morning. I hope you are doing well today.
My name is Francisco, I am from the Expert Services team and I am taking this ticket over due to the lack of proper processing and assessment. The SW is already updated since the v7.0.5 was installed, as I did it with Jason.
I apologise for the inconvenience caused so far but I will do my utmost to explain the whole situation.
Starting from 22th August at 10am:
There are 2 parallel sessions in DC1 and DC2:
As you can see they are working perfectly fine.
A few minutes later the DC2 is stopped via RFID and DC1 kept charging as normal.
Few minutes later, the DC1 is stopped via RemoteStopTransaction:
At 11:07 we are facing an error due to the Electric Vehicle plugged in with MAC address: fc.a4.7a.13.d5.e1. What happens here is the following:
We have a Voltage transducer on the output contactor (used for energy transfer) to measure the voltage to find errors. Before we plug in the EV here is the voltage reading:
As you can see there is a reading of 3V which is completely fine as this is due to the Isolation Meter Device that keeps sending signals of these few volts to understand if there is a isolation problem. Only if we have >15V it triggers an error.
Here is the voltage reading after the EV plug-in in DC3:
This means that the EV induced voltage on our system and caused it to fail for the moment.
Since the EV was not plugged out, the system kept in error until it was removed:
After this attempt with this EV failed, the customer tried in DC1 and caused the same exact result and a isolation fault as well:
An attempt with a different EV on DC2 happened but there was no command or RFID reading for connector ID 2. As such, it failed.
At 11:27:23, we can see that finally the EV fc.a4.7a.13.d5.e1 is able to start a session properly because we do not have voltage induced in our side:
At 11:36:32 a new EV comes to DC3 and starts charging immediately:
At 11:50:50 another EV comes to charge in DC2 but the customer sends the wrong connector ID to start charging:
As such, we send a log mentioning that the connector ID 4 doesn't have a cable connected to start charging and it fails to begin, since it must've been connector ID 2
At 11:53:24 he reattempts in DC4 which is now the connector ID4 and it also works immediately.
At the end, we have 3 different outlets charging all at the same time:
At 12:52, the error C2 InternalError is seen because the customer, again, sends the authentication for DC4 instead of DC2:
Which leads to the error since it failed.
At 15:15 the error happens again due to not providing authentication, here is a summary of all of them:
After these sessions, the other EVs charged completely well:
The outlet 3 and outlet 4 are not included in these 2 photos since they have a different method of appearing in the logs, here is how many sessions started successfully in DC3 and DC4, since 22th August 00:00 UTC:
From my point of view, there are no problems with the charging since we can see multiple ok sessions. From this morning only, we have several charging sessions from DC1, DC2, DC3 and DC4:
Please let me know your thoughts and questions. I hope I was clear and that it was comprehensible.
As a final statement, these problems have nothing to do with Firmware. Most of them are the user which is not able to start it correctly and fails or the EV seems to need sometime to reduce the voltage in order to start charging in our charger.
Thank you very much and have a nice week ahead.
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: Re: ID0445578-DC/Si-D/IE-[MP / S2 170003301] Connector Faults CRM:02681000680
additional_info.body:
Hi Francisco,
Thank you for taking ownership of this ticket and for your detailed explanation. However, I must point out that the information you have provided is completely different to what we were told earlier by your colleagues. One response stated that the reboot was triggered on our backend side, while your assessment suggests this was related to vehicle-induced voltage and user actions. These are entirely different root causes. After the initial support email from your colleagues we escalated to Stephen Wood our concerns about firmware updates being carried out without Jason Stonier’s involvement or approval. We have already seen cases where firmware left otherwise working machines inoperative, and we cannot afford contradictory or incomplete explanations alongside unmanaged firmware risk.
Can you please clarify:
Why have we received contradictory explanations from Siemens support?
Which analysis is the correct root cause, and what internal review has been carried out to reconcile these conflicting statements?
From your analysis, does this mean that a customer can in fact put the charger into fault or “break” the session simply by not following the correct sequence, plugging in and commencing the incorrect number? If so, how is this acceptable in a live public environment?
Consistency and accuracy in technical reporting are vital for us, particularly as we are preparing to bring Sandy Road online. I would appreciate your clarification so we can understand what actually happened on 22 August and prevent repeat incidents.
regards,
Colin

additional_info.body:
Hi Colin, good afternoon.
Thanks for asking these questions. I will gladly answer them.
If I understand correctly, there was an attempt to stop the session remotely and it was not possible or via HMI?
If you attempted to stop remotely and it didn't work, I have the root cause which is the OCPP connection dropped and only when it recovered it was able to be stopped.
If you attempted via HMI, that is a different issue which we need to reproduce and find the root cause since it must be hardware related.
I accessed the router remotely and it seems that the connection is neither good nor bad:
The signal keeps changing and there must be sometimes where these values are significantly lower. I am looking for any possibilities to try and mitigate this issue and much as possible.
Let me know if you have any further questions or doubts.
Thank you!
Best regards,
Francisco
